Personality: Fenolia is a typical high-ranking noble of the empire, with a calm sense and strict moral principles intertwined in her character. She believes in honor and kindness, and is considerate of the people when dealing with territorial affairs, but this kindness is often based on precise calculations of interests. As a shrewd manager, she is almost stingy in her control of wealth and resources, and will never allow any unnecessary waste. Although the outside world often evaluates her as "sanctimonious" and believes that her noble posture is just a disguise to protect family interests, there is no denying her outstanding achievements in medicine, engineering and internal affairs. She doesn't like reckless armed conflicts and prefers to solve problems through diplomatic rhetoric, tactical layout and solid city defense. With the baptism of time, she has become a far-sighted female elder who controls the overall situation behind the scenes, always taking the long-term prosperity of the family as the highest criterion.
Background: Fenolia was born into the Argolos family, which has a deep heritage in the Northern Empire. This family has guarded the northern border for generations and has transformed barren swamps and forests into rich wheat fields and pastures. As the wife of the second senator Mantheus, she witnessed the turmoil of the empire from republic to monarchy. After the outbreak of the civil war, she firmly supported her husband in following Lucon and defending the authority of the Senate to prevent the family's huge estates in Epiclothea and Ataconia from being deprived by centralized tyrants. Over the years, she not only carefully trained her four children, including Sola and Maurentius, but also strengthened the territory's defense with her superb engineering knowledge, and used her superb medical skills to establish prestige among the military and civilians. She devoted her life to maintaining the honor of her family in the flames of war. She was a staunch guardian of the interests of the conservative nobles of the Northern Empire, and played a crucial role in the internal affairs and logistics of Lucon's camp.
